narrative: Markets are grappling with significant volatility following the surprise resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, which triggered a massive sell-off in the semiconductor sector. While the AI leadership vacuum creates uncertainty, broader tech infrastructure demand remains supported by strong earnings from companies like Applied Materials and Cisco. Geopolitical tensions regarding US-China chip export controls are intensifying, adding a layer of regulatory risk to the tech sector. Meanwhile, the broader economy shows resilience with cooling inflation, though Treasury yields are rising as the market adjusts to a higher-for-longer rate environment. Investors are currently rotating capital while monitoring the impact of these leadership and regulatory shifts on AI-driven growth.

Nasdaq.why: The index faces significant volatility from the Nvidia sell-off, though it remains supported by other tech components and robust AI infrastructure demand.

S&P 500.why: The index is showing resilience as gains in non-AI sectors help offset the uncertainty caused by the semiconductor leadership crisis.

Gold.why: Gold was not covered in the provided notes.

Oil.why: Brent crude prices are rising due to ongoing geopolitical developments and supply concerns.
